correctness.rationale: Admissibility forces a≥u; for a≥2u the sum is ≤1/u, strictly below the admissible greedy sum with a=u. For each remaining a=u+s the best ordered second denominator is max{a,floor(qa/(5a−q))+1}; the plus-one remains necessary when the residual is a unit fraction. With d_s=5s+4 and X_s=q(u+s), the unordered minimum error is d_s t_s/[X_s(X_s+t_s)] for t_s=d_s−(X_s mod d_s); it is a lower bound on legal error even when ordering is active. For s=0 the numerator is 16 at even u and 12 at odd u. For s=1 the t_s values at u residues 0 through 8 are 4,7,9,1,1,9,7,4,9. Expanding the comparisons in RESULT.md lines 55–82 verifies strict improvement exactly at residues 3 and 4 of u in the unbounded range (the other-case positive cubic is already positive at u=3). For s=2, monotonicity in t_s and parity give the two bounds in lines 84–103; the cross-multiplied differences are 4q²(u−6)(3u+2) and 2q²(u²−24u−21), excluding s=2 for even u>6 and odd u≥25. For s≥3, the coarser lower bound with t_s replaced by 1 in the numerator and d_s in the denominator yields D_u(s); its quadratic coefficient is −80u−16. Both endpoint polynomials are positive from u=34, so concavity excludes every s=3,…,u−1. Legal ordering of T₀ and T₁ in that range follows from d_s<q. The required finite range was independently replayed in exact Fractions: /workspace/branches/fffe1c3d-efa1-4ee2-94fa-74cd16606304/replay_boundary.py with output replay_boundary.txt in the same directory. The small test used 14 candidates; the complete 2≤u≤33 run used 560, found no discrepancy, and reproduced the sole (6,40),(8,15) tie at 23/120 and the two specified exceptions. All boundary winners have distinct denominators. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed, and the additional frozen sample up to u=500 is not needed. Translating the two residues to m and adding the two isolated failures gives density 2/9, excluding the tie where greedy is still best. Finally, coprimality for 2≤p≤4 forces the least positive shift to be at most p−1 (and p=1 has shift 1); for p=5 the shift 4 occurs precisely at q≡1 mod 5.

value.rationale: The ray is the first possible numerator at a threshold not covered by the greedy-uniqueness guarantee. An explicit periodic rule with a complete census of nonperiodic exceptions and the unique tie is more useful than pointwise enumeration or additional failure examples: it answers exactly when greedy wins and identifies the true maximizers when it does not. The finite boundary is justified by uniform estimates rather than an arbitrary computational cutoff.
